events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Mitchell; Howard; Winneshiek; Allamakee; Dodge; Olmsted; Winona; Mower; Fillmore; Houston; La Crosse; Monroe; Vernon; Crawford; Richland; Grant
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In northeast Iowa, Allamakee, Howard, Mitchell and
Winneshiek Counties. In southeast Minnesota, Dodge, Fillmore,
Houston, Mower, Olmsted and Winona Counties. In Wisconsin,
Crawford, Grant, La Crosse, Monroe, Richland and Vernon Counties.

* WHEN...From this evening through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread rain is expected to develop across the region today
and continue into the day Saturday. Some locations may see
multiple inches of rainfall, particularly along and south of
Interstate 90 and north of Highway 18.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Roane; Wirt; Calhoun; Clay; Braxton; Gilmer
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Locations impacted include...
Spencer, Sutton, Gassaway, Arnoldsburg, Big Otter, Harrison, Reedy,
Nebo, Shock, Frametown, Millstone, Strange Creek, Wilsie, Tariff,
Servia, Rosedale, Orma, Lucille, Nicut, and Chloe.

This includes Interstate 79 between mile markers 36 and 64.

Heavy rain may cause ponding of water on roadways and flooding in
low-lying areas.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to travel across
flooded roads. Find alternate routes. It takes only a few inches of
swiftly flowing water to carry vehicles away.

Madison-Warren County line to the Des Moines River.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

Norwalk and threatens several rural gravel roads.

morning to a crest of 22.2 feet this afternoon. It will then fall
below flood stage late tomorrow morning.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Little Belt and Highwood Mountains; Big Belt, Bridger and Castle Mountains; Elkhorn and Boulder Mountains; Gallatin Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Horse Gulch area and burn scars from the
summer of 2026.

* WHERE...Portions of central and southwest Montana, including the
following areas, in central Montana, Big Belt, Bridger and Castle
Mountains, Elkhorn and Boulder Mountains and Little Belt and
Highwood Mountains. In southwest Montana, Gallatin Valley.

* WHEN...From this evening through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Horse Gulch and Burn Scars of
2026 is expected up to and during the period of the watch.
Residents near he Horse Gulch area and burn scars from the summer
of 2026 should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure to stay
up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall
could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized street
flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over recent burn scars, which may lead to flash flooding
and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Areas near recent burn scars from the summer 2026 and the Horse
Gulch area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

continue to be possible over the Sand Creek and Bobcat Lakes Burn
Scars.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Montana, including the following
area, Northwest Beaverhead County.

* WHEN...From 3 PM MDT this afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Sand Creek and Bobcat Lakes Burn
Scars is expected up to and during the period of the watch.
Residents near the Sand Creek and Bobcat Lakes Burn Scars should
prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with
information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger
flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized street flooding, and
debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms capable of producing locally intense
rainfall are forecast to develop over the burn scar late this
afternoon through this evening with additional precipitation
expected through Saturday, which may lead to flash flooding and
debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Areas near the Sand Creek and Bobcat Lakes Burn Scars, including
portions of the Pioneer Mountains Scenic Byway.
